classification.difficultyReason: Sketch six factorised quadratics, select the appropriate sign regions and independently confirm each solution using test values.

children.prompt: Sketch the associated parabola and hence solve:

answer.worked: The parabola $y=(x+2)(x-4)$ opens upwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-2$ and $4$. It lies below the axis between these zeroes. Hence $-2<x<4$.

answer.worked: The parabola $y=(3-x)(x+1)$ opens downwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-1$ and $3$. It lies above the axis between these zeroes. Hence $-1<x<3$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch of the associated downward parabola.
spec.mathematics: y=(3-x)(x+1), roots -1 and 3, y-intercept 3, vertex (1,4). No grid is required.

answer.worked: The parabola $y=(2-x)(x-5)$ opens downwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $2$ and $5$. It lies on or below the axis outside the zeroes, including both endpoints. Hence $x\le 2$ or $x\ge 5$.

answer.worked: The parabola $y=(x+1)(x+3)$ opens upwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-3$ and $-1$. It lies on or above the axis outside the zeroes, including both endpoints. Hence $x\le -3$ or $x\ge -1$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch of the associated upward parabola.

answer.worked: The parabola $y=(x+1)(1-x)$ opens downwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-1$ and $1$. It lies below the axis outside these zeroes. Hence $x<-1$ or $x>1$.

answer.worked: The parabola $y=(x+1)(x+2)$ opens upwards and crosses the $x$-axis at $-2$ and $-1$. It lies on or below the axis between the zeroes, including both endpoints. Hence $-2\le x\le -1$.
